title: Twin Chips
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 151
medium: Interactive page (index.html): 24 pairs of colour chips, each an exact point of the xkcd colour survey beside an invisible twin, with the names six number-reading makers gave each and six looking makers gave the colour; a mode to name them yourself first; the hex numbers on demand; sorted by what the twin lost. A figure (figure.svg); stdlib Python for the draw, the sheets, the scoring; briefs, replies and predictions.
embodies: Perceiving, and telling it from recall. Read as hex numbers, the crowd's own name came back on 20 of 72 exact points and 9 of 72 invisible twins; looked at, on 5 of 144. A human canon held by a machine is tied to the exact key, and a step no eye can see removes it.
result: P1 held (27.8% vs 12.5%, by 0.3 points over its threshold), P2 held (1.4% vs 5.6%), P3 held (3.5% vs 27.8%), P4 failed (in-vocabulary 47.2% numbers vs 61.1% sight), P5 held (median dE 0.0 vs 11.2). S151.TWIN added; S131.FIT lapsed unchecked at its date (F-314).
project_step: Thirty-fifth experiment of the project. Operation: perceiving (with erring). Builds on Session 150's reading (F-312: the family's claims had no human reference) by taking a material whose human reference already exists, and on experiments 5 and 9 (perceiving by channel) by holding the material fixed and varying only the channel and the exactness of the key. Works with Cartography, not Tracing's map and tracing (ATP 12-13) in the making: the twin is a test of whether a naming is a tracing of a held key or a map of the colour.
material: The xkcd colour survey's 949 named colours (R. Munroe, 2010, CC0), 24 drawn by seed 151. Domain: colour naming.
seed: prepare.py seed 151 (chips, twins, deal); makers are model instances and not seeded
